content.value_statement: Medical device teams need clear FDA pathways, QSR controls, HIPAA safeguards, and submission planning. This skill structures regulatory decisions, compliance checks, and inspection preparation for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Frames FDA pathway decisions for 510(k), PMA, De Novo, and pre-submission planning.
Organizes QSR topics including design controls, management responsibility, document control, and CAPA.
Outlines FDA submission preparation steps for device descriptions, indications, testing, labeling, and review responses.
Maps HIPAA safeguards for devices and systems that handle protected health information.
Summarizes cybersecurity planning needs for premarket and post-market medical device obligations.
Supports inspection readiness and warning letter response planning with structured review steps.
limitations: It provides regulatory guidance, not legal advice or an FDA determination.
It does not submit filings, contact FDA, or validate records against live agency systems.
Users must verify current rules with official FDA, HHS, and legal sources.
Several named scripts, templates, and reference files are described but not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Select a Submission Pathway
use_cases.description: Compare 510(k), PMA, De Novo, and Q-Sub options before building a submission plan.

use_cases.title: Review Quality System Gaps
use_cases.description: Translate QSR topics into a practical review plan for design controls, CAPA, documents, and management review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Connected Device Controls
use_cases.description: Plan HIPAA safeguards and FDA cybersecurity documentation for software-enabled medical devices.

prompt_templates.title: Identify My FDA Pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as my FDA regulatory planning assistant. Based on this device description, intended use, patient population, and known predicates, outline likely FDA pathways and the evidence I need next.

prompt_templates.title: Build a QSR Gap Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current quality system summary against QSR topics in this skill. Create a prioritized gap list for design controls, document controls, CAPA, and management responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Plan HIPAA and Cybersecurity Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: For this connected medical device workflow, map PHI data flows, HIPAA safeguards, cybersecurity controls, SBOM needs, and post-market vulnerability management evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare FDA Review Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this FDA request for additional information to create a response strategy, owner list, evidence plan, risk concerns, and timeline for a complete reply.

output_examples.input: A Class II monitoring device team needs to decide whether a 510(k) is realistic.
output_examples.output: A pathway memo with classification questions, predicate search tasks, substantial equivalence concerns, testing evidence, and Q-Sub decision points.

output_examples.input: A quality lead wants to prepare for an FDA inspection in six weeks.
output_examples.output: An inspection readiness plan covering document review, CAPA sampling, training records, mock inspection roles, and response preparation.

output_examples.input: A software device stores patient measurements in a cloud service.
output_examples.output: A controls checklist for PHI data flows, access management, encryption, audit logging, breach response, SBOM, and vulnerability handling.

best_practices: Provide device class, intended use, patient population, software features, predicates, and market history before asking for pathway advice.
Use outputs as planning drafts and confirm final positions with regulatory counsel and official FDA guidance.
Ask for assumptions, evidence gaps, and owner assignments so the response can support real project work.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the output as legal advice or a guaranteed FDA decision.
Do not omit adverse data, cybersecurity risks, or quality system gaps when requesting a review.
Do not rely on outdated guidance without checking current FDA and HHS sources.

faq.question: Can this skill choose the final FDA pathway for my device?
faq.answer: It can structure pathway analysis and identify evidence needs. Final decisions require official guidance, expert review, and company accountability.

faq.question: Does it support 510(k), PMA, and De Novo planning?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers these pathways and helps compare submission expectations, risks, and preparation tasks.

faq.question: Can it review HIPAA concerns for connected devices?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map PHI flows, safeguards, access controls, breach planning, and business associate considerations.

faq.question: Does the package include working FDA automation scripts?
faq.answer: No. The current package includes placeholder files and describes planned resources that are not fully included.

faq.question: Is it useful for FDA inspection readiness?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize document review, training checks, mock inspection preparation, and response planning.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
